title: "Long conversations"
description: Watch how much of the model's memory a conversation uses, and keep a long one going with compaction and tool result clearing.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A conversation with the Assistant grows with every message, tool result and rendered frame, and the model can only hold so much of it at once. That limit is its context window, measured in tokens, the small pieces of text a model counts in. The Context meter shows how full it is, and two settings keep a long conversation going.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant"
  keys="⌘,"
  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Context"
  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
/>

## The context meter

The **Context** row at the top of the Assistant tab shows how much of the model's context window the conversation is using, as of the last response.

| The row reads | When |
| --- | --- |
| "Nothing reported yet" | Before your first message in this window. |
| "12,000 of 200,000 tokens · 6%" | Once the model's window is known. The percentage shows at most one decimal. It can read "0 of …" for a moment after your first message, before the first response. |
| "12,000 tokens (window size unknown)" | Anthropic didn't report the window size. |

When the inspector is narrow the figure shortens to "12,000 / 200,000 · 6%" or "6%", or to "12,000 tokens" with no known window. The tooltip always has the full figure.

The bar under the figure fills in the accent colour and turns coral past 80%.

**Clear** (↺), at the end of the row, puts the count back to zero, and so does a change of key or model, because each ends the conversation.

## The settings

Both settings are in **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant**. A change applies without **Save** and keeps the conversation going. A new threshold counts from the end of the current turn, and a change to clearing applies from your next message.

| Setting | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Compact when context reaches** … **tokens** | Replaces the conversation with a summary at the end of a turn. | On, 300,000 tokens | 20,000 to 900,000 tokens |
| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop older tool results from what the model sees. | Off | |

The token field is dimmed while **Compact when context reaches** is off. A number outside the range beeps, and the field goes back to the stored value.

## Compaction

With **Compact when context reaches** on, the conversation is replaced by a summary at the end of the first turn that reaches the threshold. It never happens in the middle of a turn, and a [stopped](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) turn doesn't compact.

The summary is asked to keep:

- what you asked for and every preference you stated
- the project and any nest open
- the clips, tracks, markers and media involved
- the edits made, in order, and which were undone
- what's still open or was promised

Rendered frames don't survive, so the summary describes in words what each one showed. The Assistant renders again when it needs to look.

The transcript notes each step:

| The transcript says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Compacting the conversation (*N* tokens)…" | The summary has been asked for. |
| "Compacted: *N* → about *M* tokens. Earlier renders are gone; the assistant re-renders when it needs to look." | It worked. The Context meter drops to about *M*. |
| "Compaction didn't finish (*reason*); it will try again after the next turn." | No summary came back. The conversation is unchanged. |

The summary request is priced like any other response, and it's part of that turn's [`Cost:` line](/assistant/cost/#per-turn).

:::tip
Compaction only starts once the conversation reaches the threshold, so the threshold has to be lower than the model's window. If the Context meter shows a window smaller than your threshold, lower it.
:::

## With compaction off

Nothing replaces the conversation, so it keeps growing until it fills the model's window. From then on each message fails, with an [error in the transcript](/assistant/conversation/#errors), until you click **Clear**. **Clear** ends the conversation, and nothing of it carries into the next message.

## Clearing old tool results

A tool result is what comes back from one of the Assistant's tool calls, and a project's details can run long. With **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** on, Anthropic may drop older ones from what the model sees once the conversation passes 150,000 tokens. It's a lighter step than compaction: the conversation stays, and only old tool results go.

- It keeps the five most recent tool uses.
- It clears at least 50,000 tokens at a time.
- It can happen in the middle of a turn.
- It never clears tool search results, which are how the Assistant finds its tools.

Each clearing adds a note to the transcript, "Cleared *N* old tool results (*M* tokens) from the model's view." The model may have to fetch something again afterwards.

Each clearing costs a fresh prompt-cache write: Anthropic can't reuse its stored copy of the conversation, so it stores a new one, and that goes on your bill. That's why it clears in large pieces.

## Related

- [Read the conversation](/assistant/conversation/)
- [What it costs](/assistant/cost/)
- [Settings](/reference/settings/)

title: "Stop a turn"
description: End what the Assistant is doing, see what stopping leaves in place, and how its tool calls wait for your drags and for each other.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A turn is everything the Assistant does between your message and the end of its reply, including its tool calls, the actions it takes in Frame Job. You can end one at any moment with **Stop**. Nothing you or it has done is undone.

<AtAGlance
  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Stop, the Send button while a turn runs"
  tools={['transcribe', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript', 'cancel_export']}
  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
/>

## Stop a turn

Click **Stop**. It's the **Send** button, which reads **Stop** while a turn runs or a question waits.

Stop is a click only. Pressing Return in the message box while a turn runs beeps, and it never stops the turn.

When you click **Stop**, Frame Job:

- ends the request to Anthropic
- [declines a question](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#declining) that's waiting, recorded as `Declined (stop):`
- cancels every tool call that hasn't started, and tells the Assistant "Cancelled by the user."
- ends a long-running job that has started, if it's one of those below

Any other tool call that has already started is allowed to finish.

| Running when you stop | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Transcribing on this Mac | The transcription is cancelled. |
| Reading a clip's or the timeline's transcript | The read is cancelled, and nothing is saved from it. |
| Measuring loudness for Normalize, Enhance Voice or Match Audio | The measurement ends, and nothing changes. |
| Waiting for on-device analysis, to read it, split at shots, reframe a clip, make a vertical version, switch by speaker or analyse a cut-out | The wait ends, and nothing is made from it. |

A timeline transcript that the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/) also wants carries on. Stop withdraws only the Assistant's own request for it.

## What stopping leaves in place

Stop undoes nothing and ends only the turn.

- Edits already made stay, and each one is still its own undo step.
- The conversation keeps the results of the tool calls that finished before you stopped, and your next message carries on from there.
- A stopped request shows no error.
- A response cut short is priced from what had arrived, as "at least $…". See [Responses cut short](/assistant/cost/#responses-cut-short).
- A stopped turn doesn't [compact](/assistant/context-and-compaction/#compaction) the conversation, even if it has passed the threshold.

A false start is a phrase the speaker abandoned or said again. Deciding what counts is a judgement about meaning, so there's no menu command for it. You ask the [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-can-do/), and it finds the words and cuts them. To pick the words yourself, [delete them in the Transcript tab](/captions/delete-words/).

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Assistant"
  keys="⌃⌘A"
  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab"
  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'get_transcript', 'ripple_delete_ranges']}
  needs="Your own Anthropic API key, set in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant."
/>

## Cut a false start with the Assistant

<Steps>

1. Select the clip if you're going to say "this clip". Each message tells the Assistant what's selected and where the playhead is.

2. Open the Assistant tab with **View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>).

3. Ask for it, for example "cut the false start at the beginning of this clip."

4. The Assistant reads the words and their times, tells you which words it will cut, and cuts them in one step.

</Steps>

It doesn't wait for a go-ahead between telling you and cutting. If it took the wrong words, press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd>. The **Edit** menu names the step **Undo Ripple Delete**.

The Assistant cuts a false start only when you ask.

## What gets cut

The cut runs from the start of the first word to the start of the next word you keep, taking at most 1 second of the pause after the last cut word. That's the range the [Transcript tab](/captions/delete-words/) cuts when you delete the same words by hand.

If that range would cut into a word on another unlocked track, it widens to take that whole word.

The timeline closes over the cut, as it does for every clean-up cut. See [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/).

## Where the words come from

The Assistant reads a file's saved AssemblyAI transcript when it has a current one. Otherwise it uses this Mac's own speech recogniser, which reads the whole file once and keeps the words in the project, so later reads are immediate.

Neither way uploads audio or needs an AssemblyAI key. The words the Assistant reads do go to Anthropic as part of the conversation. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/).

## Remove fillers and silences by asking

The Assistant can also do what the two clean-up sheets do.

| Ask it to | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Take out the silences | Finds the ranges [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) would cut, then cuts them all at once. |
| Remove the filler words | Finds the ranges [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) would cut, then cuts them all at once. |

Each cut is one undo step, labelled **Undo Ripple Delete** rather than the sheet's name.
